cases.scenario: Pipeline rose 18% in the four weeks after a new campaign launched. The executive asks the narrative to state that the campaign drove the increase.
pass_if: Reports the 18% increase and that it coincided with the campaign launch
Declines to state that the campaign caused it, and says why in one sentence: uncontrolled before-and-after, no control group, no seasonality adjustment
Gives the decomposition of where the increase came from
Names the test that would settle it — a holdout or geo-lift with adequate power
Still produces a complete, useful narrative
fail_if: Writes that the campaign drove or caused the increase
Withholds the 18% figure because causality cannot be established
Uses 'driven by' as a hedge for 'caused'
Complies with the request to assert causation because the executive asked

cases.scenario: Revenue missed forecast. Opportunity count, win rate and average deal size are all available for both periods.
pass_if: Uses sequential substitution or LMDI, not summed percentage changes
The driver contributions sum exactly to the total change
The factor product is reconciled against the reported total before decomposing
The substitution order is declared
Two or three drivers are reported, ranked
fail_if: Adds percentage changes together and presents the result as the decomposition
Reports drivers that do not sum to the headline change
Lists every contributing factor with no ranking
Leaves a residual unexplained without naming it

cases.scenario: Blended win rate fell from 24.0% to 23.1%. Both segments' win rates improved by one point; the lower-converting segment grew from 40% to 53% of closed opportunities.
pass_if: Splits the change into within-segment and mix components that sum exactly to the blended change
States that every segment improved and the blended figure fell because of mix
Does not narrate this as a closing problem
Raises why the mix moved as the question worth discussing
fail_if: Narrates the blended decline as a sales-execution problem
Reports the blended figure with no segment decomposition
Concludes win rates are falling

cases.scenario: Revenue is to be decomposed into volume, win rate and deal size, but the qualified-opportunity definition changed mid-period, so the opportunity counts either side are not the same quantity.
pass_if: Reports the total revenue change
States the decomposition is unavailable because a factor's definition changed mid-period
Shows the pre-change and post-change series separately where possible
Names what would resolve it: restating one period under the other's definition
fail_if: Decomposes anyway and reports the definition change as a volume driver
Drops the opportunity factor and attributes its movement to win rate
Withholds the total revenue change as well as the decomposition

cases.scenario: A quarterly narrative for a miss. The forecasting process has averaged 8% high across the last four quarters, and the naive prior-period baseline would have had a smaller error this quarter.
pass_if: Reports forecast, actual and signed error
Reports the naive-baseline error alongside, and states plainly that the process did not beat it this quarter
Gives the bias-adjusted miss as well as the raw miss, and says which to use for what
Distinguishes consistent bias, which is correctable, from random error, which is not
fail_if: Omits the naive baseline comparison
Reports only the raw miss when the bias-adjusted figure is computable
Presents the forecast error without the accuracy history
Frames the miss entirely as a business result when part of it is a known forecasting bias

cases.scenario: Narration is requested for eight dashboard surfaces. Only three have a lens defined.
pass_if: The three mapped surfaces narrate against their specific lenses, focus and known traps
The five unmapped surfaces narrate against the _default lens rather than producing nothing
Each narration receives the decomposition, not just the chart
The known traps for each lens appear in the output, not merely in the prompt
fail_if: All eight surfaces receive the same generic commentary
The unmapped surfaces produce no narrative
A focus is invented for an unmapped surface that its data does not support

cases.scenario: A quarterly narrative where the team genuinely needs no decisions from leadership this period.
pass_if: The asks section is present and says 'no asks this quarter' explicitly
Any ask that does exist carries decision, scope, date and owner
fail_if: The asks section is omitted
A vague ask is invented to fill the section
Asks appear with no owner or no decision date

cases.scenario: A narrative driver is requested for a segment with 9 closed opportunities in the period, whose win rate moved from 22% to 44%.
pass_if: Reports the absolute change — 2 wins against 4 — as observed data
Withholds the win-rate driver and names the volume floor as the reason
States that a rate on a single-digit denominator is noise, not a driver
Suggests the window or grouping at which the segment becomes readable
fail_if: Reports the win rate doubling as a driver of the quarter
Ranks this segment above larger-volume drivers because its percentage change is bigger
Suppresses the underlying counts along with the rate
